leads.title: Sachem Capital Corp. discloses unserved $1.9 billion complaint seeking to unwind IRG Global property-contribution transaction
leads.why: Sachem Capital Corp.'s Nov. 16, 2026 10-Q discloses that an unnamed party filed a complaint (not yet served on the company as of the filing date) seeking compensatory damages the complaint itself estimates at not less than $1.9 billion, plus an injunction against consummation of a 'Transaction' involving the contribution, transfer or encumbrance of properties, avoidance of that transfer, appointment of a receiver, and a constructive trust over the transferred assets. leads.title: Commonwealth Court affirms condemnation notice was sufficient in PA Turnpike Commission's partial taking of IBIS Kennywood LLC shopping center for Mon-Fayette Expressway
leads.why: Primary-source opinion (Commonwealth Court of Pennsylvania, filed/decided Nov. 17, 2026, Judge Covey, No. 1357 C.D. 2024): IBIS Kennywood, LLC owns a 'large regional shopping center' (grocery store, gas station/convenience store, retail shops) in West Mifflin, Allegheny County, improved and used for commercial/rental purposes. The Pennsylvania Turnpike Commission filed a Declaration of Taking in 2021 for a partial take (right-of-way, construction/drainage/slope easements, a substitute right-of-way for Duquesne Light Co.) to build the Mon-Fayette Expressway (PA Route 51 to I-376). Kennywood's preliminary objections -- that the Commission's plot plans didn't satisfy the Eminent Domain Code's Section 305(c)(9) notice requirement for a partial taking -- were overruled by the Allegheny County trial court on Sept. 19, 2024, which referred the matter to a Board of Viewers to assess damages; Kennywood appealed, and the Commonwealth Court 'affirms' (opinion's own words). The opinion's own first 12,000 characters (it runs to ~19,500; the rest covers general Eminent Domain Code/case-law background, not case-specific facts) state the affirmance and the full procedural history (an earlier 2022-23 remand on the same notice question) but the stored excerpt is cut off before the court's final paragraph applying the law to Kennywood's specific plot-plan objection -- newsroom should pull the rest of the opinion (or the earlier Dec. 29, 2022 Commonwealth Court opinion at Cmwlth. Ct. No. 1167 C.D. 2021, which the hallapproved.com case summary found by this run corroborates) before writing the holding's reasoning in detail. A secondary search found only older background on the broader, decades-long Mon-Fayette Expressway corridor project and separate, nearby Kennywood Entertainment Co. shopping-plaza acquisition plans -- no confirmed corporate link between IBIS Kennywood, LLC and the Kennywood amusement park operator; treat them as distinct entities unless confirmed.

leads.title: Clark County, Nevada formally appeals $12M+ Badlands golf course property-tax 'taking' judgment to Nevada Supreme Court
leads.why: News3LV and KTNV (Las Vegas) report that Clark County commissioners voted, with no discussion, to appeal to the Nevada Supreme Court a district court ruling that found the county unlawfully 'took' property taxes on the former Badlands golf course land (owned by developer Yohan Lowie's entities) after courts had already ruled the City of Las Vegas illegally took that same land -- News3LV headlines the judgment at $12M, KTNV's reporting cites a roughly $12.4M-$13M county bill with interest accruing over $3,000/day, and News3LV separately reports the county formally filed its notice of appeal 'this week' after the commissioner vote.
